subject: Mediations: Discrepancies in p-values of Indirect Effects using Lavaan and Mediation package

messages.author: 8e8e14dc05c49189
messages.subject: Mediations: Discrepancies in p-values of Indirect Effects using Lavaan and Mediation package
parts:
Hi there, 

I have run some simple mediation models with a binary IV and with continuous covariate, mediator, and DV. Prior to learning about the lavaan package, I ran the model with the mediation package. 

I've compared the results between both packages, and the results are nearly identical (e.g., same coefficient estimates), but the p-values for the indirect effect differ, even though the coefficient estimates are the same and the p-values for the other effects are the same. 

I'm using the bootstrapping technique in both packages, and have tried running the code with varying randomization seeds as well as number of simulations. Regardless, the same pattern is persisting. Below is the code I'm using and results. Has anyone encountered a similar situation? Is there an additional specifier I need to be adding to calculated the indirect effect accurately in lavaan? 


library(lavaan)

sem_model = '
att_neg ~ a*group + chi_beh_control 
avs_rpm_epi ~ c*group + chi_beh_control + b*att_neg
 

direct := c
 
#indirect effect
indirect := a*b
 
#total effect
total := c + (a*b)
'

set.seed(567)
model_sem2 = sem(sem_model, data=nona_data, se="bootstrap", test="bootstrap", bootstrap=1000) 



The code used in the Mediation package & output is below:

med_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na <- lm(att_neg ~ group + chi_beh_control, data = nona_data)
out_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na <- lm(avs_rpm_epi ~ group + chi_beh_control + att_neg, data = nona_data) 
set.seed(567)
med_out_avs_rpm_epi_na <- mediate(med_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na, out_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na, boot = TRUE, treat = "group", mediator = "att_neg", sims = 1000)
summary(med_out_avs_rpm_epi_na)

the ACME, ADE, and total effect estimates are the same as from the lavaan package, but the p-value differs significantly. 
(ACME = average causal mediation effects/indirect effects)

Thank you!

parts:
Ah, I didn't catch se="bootstrap" that Rakoon spotted. Yes, that does not return the percentile bootstrap--it just computes the SE without parametric assumptions . The confidence intervals returned are symmetric, which is not going to be the most apt for indirect effects.

And I agree with Rakoon that it's unusual for journals to request p-values with percentile bootstrap CIs.

On Fri, Aug 28, 2020 at 10:33 AM krmu...@gmail.com <krmu...@gmail.com> wrote:

Got it, thank you both that's really helpful. I don't see the CIs in my output, so would I need to run separate code like this to calculate the CIs: parameterestimates(fsem1, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple", standardized = TRUE) ? this code is from https://nmmichalak.github.io/nicholas_michalak/blog_entries/2018/nrg01/nrg01.html?

On Thursday, August 27, 2020 at 11:40:52 PM UTC-5 Rakoon P wrote:
Not sure about your situation, but in my area I believe reviewers mainly want to see that the bootstrapped SE do not contain zero and the p-values of indirect effects do not get reported.

On Thursday, August 27, 2020 at 11:28:49 PM UTC-5 krmu...@gmail.com wrote:
Interesting! The lavaan results are different when I only use test = "bootstrap" and remove se = "bootstrap." I tried this out with a couple different seed randomizations and bootstraps. Those results match up with the results from the mediation package. I guess now I'm not quite sure whether it's more correct to include se or not.. 

On Thursday, August 27, 2020 at 10:13:38 PM UTC-5 Rakoon P wrote:
If you use  test = "bootstrap"  instead of se = "bootstrap"  , do you still get the same results?

On Thursday, August 27, 2020 at 7:18:17 PM UTC-5 krmu...@gmail.com wrote:
Thanks for the quick reply Patrick. Even when I set the bootstrap draws to 5000 in both packages, the same pattern exists..


On Thursday, August 27, 2020 at 5:55:04 PM UTC-5 mal...@malonequantitative.com wrote:
What happens if you ramp the bootstrap draws up to, say, 5000? 1000 really isn't a lot for a percentile bootstrap.

On Thu, Aug 27, 2020 at 6:45 PM krmu...@gmail.com <krmu...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi there, 

I have run some simple mediation models with a binary IV and with continuous covariate, mediator, and DV. Prior to learning about the lavaan package, I ran the model with the mediation package. 

I've compared the results between both packages, and the results are nearly identical (e.g., same coefficient estimates), but the p-values for the indirect effect differ, even though the coefficient estimates are the same and the p-values for the other effects are the same. 

I'm using the bootstrapping technique in both packages, and have tried running the code with varying randomization seeds as well as number of simulations. Regardless, the same pattern is persisting. Below is the code I'm using and results. Has anyone encountered a similar situation? Is there an additional specifier I need to be adding to calculated the indirect effect accurately in lavaan? 


library(lavaan)

sem_model = '
att_neg ~ a*group + chi_beh_control 
avs_rpm_epi ~ c*group + chi_beh_control + b*att_neg
 

direct := c
 
#indirect effect
indirect := a*b
 
#total effect
total := c + (a*b)
'

set.seed(567)
model_sem2 = sem(sem_model, data=nona_data, se="bootstrap", test="bootstrap", bootstrap=1000) 



The code used in the Mediation package & output is below:

med_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na <- lm(att_neg ~ group + chi_beh_control, data = nona_data)
out_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na <- lm(avs_rpm_epi ~ group + chi_beh_control + att_neg, data = nona_data) 
set.seed(567)
med_out_avs_rpm_epi_na <- mediate(med_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na, out_fit_avs_rpm_epi_na, boot = TRUE, treat = "group", mediator = "att_neg", sims = 1000)
summary(med_out_avs_rpm_epi_na)

the ACME, ADE, and total effect estimates are the same as from the lavaan package, but the p-value differs significantly. 
(ACME = average causal mediation effects/indirect effects)

Thank you!
